`Template.render` binds the context with `Context.bind_template` only when nothing is bound yet, so the one bound is the outermost: a template it extends or includes finds the context bound (`django/template/base.py:Template.render`).
`Context.update` pushes a mapping as a new level; unlike `dict.update`, it changes no level already there (`django/template/context.py:Context.update`).

When the render ends it empties the place again (`django/template/context.py:RequestContext.bind_template`).

`RequestContext.new` returns a context with no held place: the stack is reset to the bottom level and the values given, and the index deleted, a comment says for backwards compatibility (`django/template/context.py:RequestContext.new`).

A template included by `{% include … only %}` sees no `"csrf_token"` or `"request"`; `InclusionNode.render`, which also renders against `new`, copies `"csrf_token"` across, because, its comment says, inclusion tags are often used for forms (`django/template/library.py:InclusionNode.render`).
The backend's template wrapper makes its context with `make_context`, from the view's dictionary and the request, if any (`django/template/backends/django.py:Template.render`).
With one, it makes a `RequestContext` with no dictionary, then pushes the view's dictionary on top, unless it is empty (`django/template/context.py:make_context`).
